Hey guys, I thought I'd document my recent work with Linux and share it with you all.
As of right now, after this experimentation, I am still running Windows for my desktop needs (graphic design, gaming, sound engineering, game development) and Linux on my servers (media, web, e-mail, storage)
My main desktop looks like:
-Intel Core i5-4690K Devil's Canyon
-AMD R9 290x
-8 GB RAM
-Other things that don't really matter.

Linux-Only Performance
Games actually worked pretty well with one considerable flaw - that being that the colors were not represented properly in most games. The RadeonSI open source driver and the Catalyst driver (flgrx) performed similarly for most games, however they both had color issues. That may not be a big deal for some people but it bugged the hell out of me. Some of my important programs didn't run well in Linux. The most considerable is GIMP - Xorg decided that while working with high resolution pictures, it would eat as much CPU as possible and cause some heavy overloading.
Guild Wars 2 in Linux also sucks. I can normally run it (most of the time) at max graphics with a solid FPS. It's wine iteration is lowest graphics at around 20-30 FPS. I don't blame Linux for this, but I do play that game regularly with my wife and the sacrifice in performance is real.
Unity ran fine - but anything regarding graphics capability was considerably slower.
I decided I needed some Windows in my desktop to not tear my hair out while trying to run things.

Attempts to include a bit of Windows instead of going back to full Windows:

GPU Passthrough - Gaming
Many of you saw my post in technology showcasing the idea of GPU passthrough - basically passing your graphics card through to a VM so you can run Linux and Windows at the same time.
While I got the VM to work and the passthrough to be successful, I was unable to get my graphics card working within the VM. Regardless of my success in being able to install the driver and have the display work beautifully, the graphics card I have is not willing to work with this setup and causes constant bluescreens while trying to run games. Frustratingly so, I was unable to resolve these issues. I tried several different drivers and configurations, and came to the conclusion that my card does not like being passed through to a VM.

Dual Booting
I hate dual booting. I play games on my main computer constantly, usually in hour periods. Having to reboot constantly by demand is what I hate about dual booting, and trying to be productive with that many gaps is very frustrating to me. I honestly gave it the best shot I could, but picking and choosing which programs I used was horrible. That and the programs that were supposed to work in Linux started overloading my normally capable computer for reasons that have not been patched yet.

Conclusion:
Windows with my current setup, or Linux with an Nvidia graphics card.
Too poor right now for a new graphics card. Kid's on the way. You get it. Still with Windows. Linux still kicks butt, but not if your graphics card reads "AMD." Really hated myself for switching back, but so it goes. I can use my Windows box for production and gaming and one of my Linux boxes for anything more personal.

Wizards of the Coast Community Forums to be Shut Down | Dungeons & Dragons

The Community Forums will be shut down on October 29.

Social media has changed significantly over the last ten years, and discussions about games aren't exclusive to company-hosted forums. The majority of community conversation takes place on third-party websites (such as Reddit, Twitter, Facebook, Tumblr, and many other fantastic community-run websites), and it is up to us to evolve alongside our players.

We encourage past and current users to retrieve any information you want to retain from the Community Forums for both Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering. The shutdown will occur on October 29, 2015, at 10:00 a.m. PT. We want to provide enough time for our forum members to move their content, and we recognize that given our forum's vibrant user base and extensive history, this may take time. Any information still on the forums on the cut-off date will be deleted.
